summary: Router 0.26.0, ADR-0080 (renumbered after ADR-0076 to ADR-0079 landed on main; rebased onto main after v0.31.0, entry in the v0.31.1 row). render-env.sh (run as root by the secrets units, access file in the root-only folder of ADR-0073) additionally renders the secrets named in EXTRA_SECRET_KEYS from render-env.conf into /etc/skirnir-router/secrets.env, so a further OpenAI-compatible cloud provider (example: Mistral's EU endpoint) is configuration only. Traced: secrets.env is the EnvironmentFile of skirnir-router.service (root); cloud.py reads a provider key only from the env name in api_key_env; config.py validates base_url against the egress allowlist and HTTPS (loopback HTTP only). Controls added in the renderer: names must start with a capital letter, contain only [A-Z0-9_] (they become part of the secret-store query path) and end in _KEY or _TOKEN, so LD_PRELOAD, PATH, PYTHONPATH and similar never reach the root unit's environment; globbing is off while splitting; built-in names are not fetched twice; a missing name is reported by name only. While tracing, a pre-existing path was found and closed for every key: a secret value with LF or CR would have added a further variable of the store writer's choosing to the EnvironmentFile; such values are now refused (MQTT_PASSWORD: nothing rendered, existing file kept). config.example.yaml adds egress_allow [api.eu.mistral.ai] and a disabled mistral provider (kind openai, region eu); selftest_cloud_transport now appends to the example's egress_allow instead of replacing it. New CI test test/selftest_render_env.py runs the real script against a fake secret store (bash/curl/jq; refuses to skip in CI). Threat model EN/DE and register TM-14 updated; docs EN/DE, READMEs, CHANGELOG.

findings.evidence: secrets.env is the router unit's EnvironmentFile (root). A configurable list of names would let a name such as LD_PRELOAD or PYTHONPATH carry a secret-store value into the root process.
findings.resolution: Only names ending in _KEY or _TOKEN with [A-Z0-9_] are rendered; others are reported and skipped. The list lives in render-env.conf (root-only folder, ADR-0073), not in the router-writable config.yaml. Rejected-case test with LD_PRELOAD, PATH, PYTHONPATH; a copy of the script without the suffix rule fails it.

findings.evidence: Pre-existing: render-env.sh wrote KEY=value lines with printf without checking the value; a value with a line break from the secret store (built-in keys included) would have started a further variable in the root unit's environment.
findings.resolution: Every rendered value must be a single line (no LF/CR); otherwise the key is skipped and named, MQTT_PASSWORD keeps the existing file. Tests for a built-in key, further keys with LF and with CR, and MQTT_PASSWORD; a copy without the check fails all four tests.

findings.evidence: New log lines in the renderer name keys that are invalid, missing or multi-line.
findings.resolution: Only names are printed, never values; the test asserts that no synthetic secret value or injected fragment appears in the output.

findings.evidence: The example adds a further egress host for a disabled provider.
findings.resolution: No code change in the cloud path; base_url stays bound to the allowlist and HTTPS by config.py (selftest_cloud_transport cases unchanged). Data classes, privacy check, credential scan and budget apply to the new provider as to OpenAI. Redirect behaviour remains the existing residual risk of TM-06.

tests.command: python test/selftest_render_env.py on a Linux router host (bash/curl/jq), in /tmp with the router venv, live router untouched
tests.evidence: Ran 4 tests: OK (after the rebase onto 4176f77). Counter-checks with the same tests: script without the suffix rule FAILED (1), script whose line check always passes FAILED (4).

tests.command: All python steps of ci.yml run locally on Windows (75 commands)
tests.evidence: 74/75 ok; check_public_changes needs the CI base variable and was run separately below.

tests.command: ruff check .; python router/router.py --check router/config.example.yaml --pure; python test/check_adr_index.py; python test/check_control_flow.py; python test/selftest_threat_review.py
tests.evidence: All checks passed; configuration ok: 5 roles, 7 models; ADR index ok: 80 ADRs; control flow ok.

limitations: selftest_render_env.py skips on Windows (no bash/jq there); it ran on a Linux router host and runs in CI, where a skip is refused.
The suffix rule is a name rule: a secret the operator names with _KEY still reaches the router's environment by design.
systemd EnvironmentFile still interprets quotes and backslashes in single-line values (pre-existing, unchanged); the router reads MQTT_PASSWORD raw from the file for that reason.
Choosing a provider (terms, data retention) is the operator's decision; no request to a provider was part of these tests.
